segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Thank you very much. I'd like to thank all of the witnesses for being here today to discuss this very unique topic. And I'd like to jump right into my questions, if you don't mind: Commander Fravor, can you briefly describe your background?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yeah, I was an enlisted Marine, Naval Academy graduate, Navy, flew for 18 years, got a master's from University of Houston, and I've worked in the private sector for the last, what now? 1916 years? 17 years. I do a lot of defense work.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Really Gold plated credentials. Commander Fravor, we have all seen the floating Tic TAC video that you engaged with on November 14, 2004. Can you briefly talk about why you were off the coast of San Diego that day?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yeah, we were at a workup with all the battle groups, so we integrate the ships with the carrier, the airwing with the carrier, and we start working. So we were doing an air defense to hone not only our skills, but those of the USS Princeton when they had been tracking them for two weeks. The problem was that there was never manned aircraft airborne when they were tracking them. And this was the first day, and unfortunately, we were the ones airborne and went and saw it.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Do you remember the weather that day? Was it cloudy or windy or anything out of the ordinary on the Pacific Coast?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: It was actually, if you're familiar with San Diego, it was a perfect day. Light winds, no white caps, clear skies, not a cloud. It was for flying. It was the best.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Now, is it true that you saw, in your words, a 40 foot flying Tic TAC shaped object?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: That's correct. Or for some people that can't know what a Tic TAC is, it's a giant flying propane tank.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Fair enough. Did this object come up on radar or interfere with your radar or the USS Princeton?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: The Princeton tracked it. The Nimitz tracked it. The E two tracked it. We never saw it on our radars. Our fire control radars never picked it up. The other airplane that took the video did get it on a radar. As soon as it tried to lock it jammed the radar, spit the lock, and he rapidly switched over to the targeting pod, which you can do in the F-18.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: From what you saw that day and what you've seen on video, did you see any source of propulsion from the flying object, including on any potential thermal scans from your aircraft?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No, there's none. There's no IR plume coming out. And Chad, who took the video, went through all the EO, which is black and white TV and the IR modes, and there's no visual signs of propulsion. It's just sitting in space at 20,000ft.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: In your career, have you ever seen a propulsion system that creates no thermal exhaust?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Can you describe how the aircraft maneuvered?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Abruptly, very determinant. It knew exactly what it was doing. It was aware of our presence, and it had acceleration rates that mean it went from zero to matching our speed in no time at all.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Now, if the fastest plane on Earth was trying to do these maneuvers that you saw, would it be capable of doing that?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No, not even close.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: And just to confirm, this object had no wings, correct?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No wings.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Now, was the aircraft that you were flying, was it armed?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No. Never felt threatened at all

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: if the aircraft was armed, do you believe that your aircraft or any aircraft in possession of the United States could have shot the Tic TAC down?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I'd say no. Just on the performance. It would just left in a split second.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: It looks like we have a problem here that needs further investigation.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Yes.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: In your belief, is this flying Tic TAC, I mean, is it capable of being the product of any other nation on the Earth?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No, actually, I said like I said earlier, I think it defies current material science and the ability to develop that much propulsion. And I know there's been some physicists have done calculations, which is beyond anything that we have.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Well, either the United States has an adversary here in this world that we don't know, or we really have some serious investigations to do. I really appreciate you being here. Is there anything else about the November 14, 2004 incident that you think is important for this committee to know that you haven't been asked here today?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No. It's been said it's probably the most credible UFO sighting in history, based on all the sensors that were tracking it. And then for us to get visual and to go against the naysayers, it's something on the screen or whatever. I mean, there's four sets of human eyeballs. We're all very credible of the six of us that were involved in the thing, including the video, every one of us is going to do 20 plus years in the military in very responsible positions. So I'd say the world needs to know that it's not a joke.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Thank you very much for your testimony here today, for all of you, and I yield back, Mr. Chairman
